existing.description: The Tilburg University Waiver halves the institutional tuition fee for up to 21 non-EEA international applicants each year, as part of the university's Diversity, Equity and Inclusion commitment. It applies to all regular one-year Master's programmes starting in September 2027, with the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence as an explicit exception; Research Master's and Pre-Master's students are not eligible. Applicants must have completed their most recent degree in a designated country and must not already hold any other tuition-fee waiver. If more eligible applicants apply than there are waivers, recipients are chosen by random lottery, and outcomes are notified by 1 June 2027.
eligibility: Have completed, or be due to complete before the start of the Master's program, your most recent degree in one of the designated eligible countries
It must be your first Master's program at Tilburg University
Submit a complete application for a regular one-year Master's program starting in September 2027 by April 1, 2027
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form by April 1, 2027
Not hold any other tuition-fee waiver; the waiver cannot be combined with any other scholarship covering all or part of tuition
Not apply to a Research Master's program
Not be enrolled in, or have been enrolled in, a Pre-Master's program at Tilburg University
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a non-EEA nationality, have completed (or be due to complete before the Master's starts) their most recent degree in a designated eligible country, be applying for a regular one-year Tilburg Master's programme starting September 2027, have submitted both the programme application and the waiver form by 1 April 2027, be directly admitted rather than entering through a Pre-Master's, be in their first Master's programme at Tilburg University, and hold no other tuition-fee waiver.
benefits: 50% reduction of the institutional tuition fee
coverage: 50% reduction of the institutional tuition fee
application_method: Submit a complete application for an eligible regular one-year Master's programme starting September 2027 by 1 April 2027
Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application webform by 1 April 2027
existing.selection_notes: Selection takes place by random lottery if more eligible applicants apply than waivers available. Only applicants who are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to a Master's programme are included in the draw, so the programme application must be submitted in good time. A waiver becomes effective only after unconditional admission has been confirmed. If fewer than 21 waivers are accepted, the remaining awards are assigned by lottery to non-EEA applicants who submitted the form before 1 April 2027 and hold conditional or unconditional admission by 1 June 2027.
existing.best_fit: Non-EEA nationals whose most recent degree is from a designated eligible country, applying for a regular one-year Tilburg Master's programme starting September 2027, who need help with the tuition fee but can fund the remaining 50% and meet Dutch IND financial proof requirements.
existing.notes: The waiver is non-deferrable: deferring or withdrawing cancels the award. The two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence, including its Artificial Intelligence for Psychological Research and Artificial Intelligence en Cybersecurity tracks, is the stated exception to the one-year rule. Research Master's applicants are directed to the separate Research Master Scholarship instead.
existing.duration: One year of tuition for a regular Master's programme; the two-year Master in Cognitive Science and Artificial Intelligence is also eligible
existing.application_period: Annual for the September intake. The current cycle is the 2027-2028 academic year (21 waivers), applications open now and close 1 April 2027, with outcomes by 1 June 2027. Waivers are not available for the February intake.
existing.deadline_display: Both the Master's programme application and the waiver webform must be completed by the same date: "Submit your application for a Tilburg University Master's program by April 1, 2027" and "Complete the Tilburg University Waiver application form before April 1, 2027". Outcomes are notified by June 1, 2027.
existing.program_type: Partial tuition-fee waiver awarded by the university (DEI scheme), allocated by lottery among eligible admitted applicants

scholarships.title: TU/e Scholarship for Excellence: Shaping the Future of Microchip Innovation

existing.description: Eindhoven University of Technology awards approximately 35 Scholarship for Excellence places to international students applying to selected Master's programmes in Applied Physics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Mathematics & Computer Science for the 2027-2028 academic year. Each scholarship is worth €7,500 per academic year for two years, paid in monthly instalments, and the University states it is not a full scholarship. Consideration is part of the normal Master's application, which must be completed by 1 January 2027 with a short motivation.
eligibility: Applied for a full-time Master's programme (or an eligible track) at TU/e for the 2027-2028 academic year, starting 1 September 2027
Meet the specific admission requirements of the Master's programme applied to
Completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or university bachelor's degree, or both
Have not completed higher education (university or university of applied sciences) in the Netherlands; exchange programmes are allowed
Have excellent academic results, demonstrated by a latest grade transcript GPA of at least 7.5/10
Will meet all requirements for obtaining a Dutch entry visa and residence permit
Not applying for a joint Master's with Tilburg University (JADS) or a European Double Degree programme
Have not been admitted on the basis of an admission decision from a previous intake
existing.eligibility_summary: International applicants who have applied for an eligible full-time TU/e Master's programme for 2027-2028, meet that programme's admission requirements, completed a non-Dutch high school diploma or bachelor's degree, have no prior Dutch higher education, hold a GPA of at least 7.5/10, and can obtain a Dutch entry visa and residence permit.
benefits: €7,500 per academic year for two years
Paid in monthly instalments to a Dutch (or SEPA) bank account
Approximately 35 awards: 20 for EEA students and 15 for non-EEA students
coverage: €7,500 per academic year for two years towards study costs
requirements: Confirm in the Master's application that you wish to be considered for the scholarship
Include a brief motivation explaining why you believe you are a strong candidate
Gain at least 45 ECTS in the first year to receive the second-year scholarship
documents: Brief motivation statement within the application
application_method: Apply for the Master's programme through the regular TU/e admissions route
Tick the scholarship option and include the motivation in that application
existing.selection_notes: Very competitive: the University states only about 2% of applicants receive the award. The TU/e International Office checks eligibility, then a Selection Committee consisting of the Rector Magnificus, Dean of Education, Director Finance & Control and Director Education & Student Affairs ranks applications. Selections are confirmed by the end of March 2027.
existing.notes: The scholarships are funded by the national Beethoven Programme, a Dutch government investment in the microchip sector. For non-EEA students part of the first-year award is funded by the Dutch Ministry of Education, Culture and Science through the NL Scholarship; TU/e states you cannot apply for the NL Scholarship separately.
existing.application_period: Academic year 2027-2028, starting 1 September 2027; complete the Master's programme application by 1 January 2027.
existing.program_type: University merit scholarship (funded through the national Beethoven Programme)
